sections.heading: MECHATRONIC SYSTEMS ENGINEERING
lines: Faculty of Engineering - Mechatronic Systems Engineering

Students entering the Mechatronic Systems Engineering program must have completed the entire first year program in Engineering, with no outstanding credits to be taken, and have a Year Weighted Average (YWA) of at least 70%. First consideration will be given to applicants with a minimum grade of 60% in each of the following courses: Numerical and Mathematical Methods 1411A/B, Numerical and Mathematical Methods 1412A/B, Numerical and Mathematical Methods 1414A/B, Engineering Science 1022A/B/Y, Engineering Science 1036A/B, Engineering Science 1050, Physics 1401A/B and Physics 1402A/B.
Full-year courses: Business Administration 1299E, Engineering Science 1050.

Half-year courses: Chemistry 1302A/B, Engineering Science 1021A/B, Engineering Science 1036A/B, Numerical and Mathematical Methods 1411A/B, Numerical and Mathematical Methods 1412A/B, Numerical and Mathematical Methods 1414A/B, Physics 1401A/B and Physics 1402A/B.
(Three of the half courses are taken in each term as scheduled)

Computer Science 1037A/B, ECE 2205A/B, MME 2202A/B (or the former MSE 2212A/B), MME 2204A/B (or the former MSE 2214A/B), MME 2213A/B (or the former MSE 2213A/B), MME 2273A/B (or the former MSE 2273A/B), MSE 2200Q/R/S/T, MSE 2201A/B, MSE 2202A/B, MSE 2221A/B, MSE 2233A/B, Numerical and Mathematical Methods 2270A/B, Numerical and Mathematical Methods 2276A/B.

ECE 2277A/B, ECE 3330A/B, ECE 3331A/B, ECE 3375A/B, MME 3360A/B (or the former (MSE 3360A/B), MME 3380A/B (or the former MSE 3380A/B), MME 3381A/B (or the former MSE 3381A/B), MSE 3301A/B, MSE 3302A/B, MSE 3310A/B, Writing 2130F/G or ELI 4100F/G, 0.5 non- technical elective*.
ECE 4460A/B or ECE 4469A/B, ELI 4110F/G, MSE 4401A/B, MSE 4499, Statistical Sciences 2141A/B or Statistical Sciences 2143A/B, 1.0 non-technical elective.

*Selection of the non-technical elective must be approved by the Academic Advisor to satisfy the CEAB requirements of subject matter that deals with central issues, methodologies, and thought processes of the humanities and social sciences. An approved list can be found on the Engineering website.
